text:
Aria: Heads-up  I opened a docs PR that adds a short section on resumable streaming (cursor stitching) and clarifies differences with pagination tokens. Preview: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4012. Can folks sanity-check the language and code snippets for py/ts/go?

Ben: Nice. Quick read: we should be explicit that stream cursors are transient offsets (good for resuming a live connection) while page_token is an opaque snapshot marker for pagination. Suggest the 1-liner: "stream cursor = transient resume offset; page_token = stable pagination anchor (opaque)".

Chi: Also add a tiny warning about deduplication when resuming streams. Example: when reconnecting, the client may see the last N tokens again; recommend callers de-duplicate by token id or timestamp. I sketched a Python example:```python
# resume-aware consumer
cursor = last_seen_cursor
for chunk in client.stream_resume(cursor=cursor):
    if chunk.id == last_seen_id:
        continue  # drop duplicates
    process(chunk)
    last_seen_id = chunk.id
    cursor = chunk.cursor
```
Callout: `cursor` is advisory and may be tied to buffer/kv cache retention windows.

Aria: Good call. For TypeScript I added an async iterator example showing reconnection:```ts
let cursor = lastCursor
for await (const part of client.stream.resume({cursor})) {
  if (part.duplicate) continue
  render(part.text)
  cursor = part.cursor
}
```
And a short note: treat cursor as opaque; don't try to parse or derive semantics from it.

Ben: For Go we should show a Receive pattern that returns a cursor on each chunk and preserve ctx cancellation:```go
stream, err := client.StreamResume(ctx, &pb.ResumeReq{Cursor: cursor})
if err != nil { return err }
for {
  chunk, ok := stream.Recv()
  if !ok { break }
  if chunk.Err != nil { continue }
  // dedupe by chunk.Id if needed
  handle(chunk.Text)
  cursor = chunk.Cursor
}
```
Add: "don't assume cursors persist indefinitely; the platform may expire them."

Chi: I also added a short paragraph recommending a small client-side buffer and a dedupe window (e.g., keep last 32 ids) to handle replay on reconnect. And a tiny pseudo-example for exponential backoff when encountering RATE_LIMIT during resume attempts.

docs-bot: Preview deployed  https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/pr-4012  build passed :white_check_mark:

Aria: Thanks! Action items: Chi to add the dedupe-window note + tiny pseudocode, Ben to add the cursor-expiry sentence in the summary, I'll squash+merge after CI. Ping here if you want a final read. :wave:
